verses.text: Hæc dicit Dóminus: Vox in excélso audíta est lamentatiónis, luctus, et fletus Rachel plorántis fílios suos, et noléntis consolári super eis, quia non sunt.
Hæc dicit Dóminus: Quiéscat vox tua a plorátu, et óculi tui a lácrimis: quia est merces óperi tuo, ait Dóminus: et reverténtur de terra inimíci.
Et est spes novíssimis tuis, ait Dóminus: et reverténtur fílii ad términos suos.

responsory.text: Centum quadragínta quátuor míllia, qui empti sunt de terra, hi sunt qui cum muliéribus non sunt coinquináti:
responsory.repeat: Vírgines enim permansérunt, ídeo regnant cum Deo, et Agnus Dei cum illis.

responsory.text: Isti sunt qui venérunt ex magna tribulatióne, et lavérunt stolas suas in sánguine Agni.
Vírgines enim permansérunt, ídeo regnant cum Deo, et Agnus Dei cum illis.

parts.title: Lesson from the book of Jeremias

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord: A voice was heard on high of lamentation, of mourning, and weeping, of Rachel weeping for her children, and refusing to be comforted for them, because they are not.
Thus saith the Lord: Let thy voice cease from weeping, and thy eyes from tears: for there is a reward for thy work, saith the Lord: and they shall return out of the land of the enemy.
And here is hope for thy last end, saith the Lord: and the children shall return to their own borders.

responsory.text: A hundred forty four thousand, which were redeemed from the earth; these are they which were not defiled with women.
responsory.repeat: For they remained virgins; therefore are they kings before God, and the Lamb of God is with them.

responsory.text: These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes in the Blood of the Lamb.
For they remained virgins; therefore are they kings before God, and the Lamb of God is with them.

verses.text: Audiens audívi Ephraim transmigrántem: Castigásti me, et erudítus sum, quasi juvénculus indómitus: convérte me, et convértar: quia tu Dóminus Deus meus.
Postquam enim convertísti me, egi pœniténtiam: et postquam ostendísti mihi, percússi femur meum. Confúsus sum, et erúbui: quóniam sustínui oppróbrium adolescéntiæ meæ.
Si fílius honorábilis mihi Ephraim, si puer delicátus: quia ex quo locútus sum de eo, adhuc recordábor ejus.

responsory.text: Sub altáre Dei audívi voces occisórum dicéntium:
responsory.repeat: Quare non deféndis sánguinem nostrum? Et accepérunt divínum respónsum: Adhuc sustinéte módicum tempus, donec impleátur númerus fratrum vestrórum.

responsory.text: Vidi sub altáre Dei ánimas interfectórum propter verbum Dei, et propter testimónium quod habébant, et clamábant voce magna, dicéntes.
Quare non deféndis sánguinem nostrum? Et accepérunt divínum respónsum: Adhuc sustinéte módicum tempus, donec impleátur númerus fratrum vestrórum.

verses.text: Hearing I heard Ephraim when he went into captivity: thou hast chastised me, and I was instructed, as a young bullock unaccustomed to the yoke. Convert me, and I shall be converted, for thou art the Lord my God.
For after thou didst convert me, I did penance: and after thou didst shew unto me, I struck my thigh: I am confounded and ashamed, because I have borne the reproach of my youth.
Surely Ephraim is an honourable son to me, surely he is a tender child: for since I spoke of him, I will still remember him.

responsory.text: I heard under the altar the voices of them that were slain, saying:
responsory.repeat: How long dost Thou not avenge our blood? And it was said unto them from God: Rest yet for a little season, until the number of your brethren be fulfilled.

responsory.text: I saw under the altar of God the souls of them that were slain for the Word of God, and for the testimony which they held, and they cried with a loud voice, saying:
How long dost Thou not avenge our blood? And it was said unto them from God: Rest yet for a little season, until the number of your brethren be fulfilled.

verses.text: Státue tibi spéculam, pone tibi amaritúdines: dírige cor tuum in viam rectam, in qua ambulásti: revértere, virgo Israël, revértere ad civitátes tuas istas.
Usquequo delíciis dissólveris, fília vaga? quia creávit Dóminus novum super terram: Fémina circúmdabit virum.
Hæc dicit Dóminus exercítuum Deus Israël: Adhuc dicent verbum istud in terra Juda, et in úrbibus ejus, cum convértero captivitátem eórum: Benedícat tibi Dóminus, pulchritúdo justítiæ, mons sanctus.

responsory.text: Adoravérunt vivéntem in sǽcula sæculórum,
responsory.repeat: Mitténtes corónas suas ante thronum Dómini Dei sui.

responsory.text: Et cecidérunt in conspéctu throni in fácies suas: et benedixérunt vivéntem in sǽcula sæculórum.
Mitténtes corónas suas ante thronum Dómini Dei sui.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Mitténtes corónas suas ante thronum Dómini Dei sui.

verses.text: Set thee up a watchtower, make to thee bitterness: direct thy heart into the right way, wherein thou hast walked: return, O virgin of Israel, return to these thy cities.
How long wilt thou be dissolute in deliciousness, O wandering daughter? for the Lord hath created a new thing upon the earth: A woman shall compass a man.

Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: As yet shall they say this word in the land of Juda, and in the cities thereof, when I shall bring back their captivity: The Lord bless thee, the beauty of justice, the holy mountain.

responsory.text: They worshipped Him That liveth for ever and ever.
responsory.repeat: And cast their crowns before the throne of the Lord their God.

responsory.text: And they fell down upon their faces before the throne, and blessed Him That liveth for ever and ever.
And cast their crowns before the throne of the Lord their God.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
And cast their crowns before the throne of the Lord their God.

parts.title: Sermo sancti Augustíni Epíscopi
paragraphs: Hódie, fratres caríssimi, natálem illórum infántium cólimus, quos ab Heróde crudelíssimo rege interféctos esse, Evangélii textus elóquitur. Et ídeo cum summa exsultatióne gáudeat terra, cæléstium mílitum et tantárum parens fecúnda virtútum. Ecce profánus hostis nunquam beátis párvulis tantum prodésse potuísset obséquio, quantum prófuit ódio. Nam, sicut sacratíssimum præséntis diéi festum maniféstat, quantum in beátos párvulos iníquitas abundávit, tantum in eis grátia benedictiónis refúdit.

responsory.text: Effudérunt sánguinem Sanctórum velut aquam in circúitu Jerúsalem:
Posuérunt mortália servórum tuórum escas volatílibus cæli, carnes sanctórum tuórum béstiis terræ.
Et non erat qui sepelíret.

parts.title: From the Sermons of St. Augustine, Bishop (of Hippo)
paragraphs: Dearly beloved brethren, today we keep the birthday of those children, who, as we are informed by the Gospel, were massacred by the savage King Herod. Therefore let earth rejoice with exceeding joy, for she is the mother of these heavenly soldiers, and of this numerous host. The love of the vile Herod could never have crowned these blessed ones as hath his hatred. For the Church testifieth by this holy solemnity, that whereas iniquity did specially abound against these little saints, so much the more were heavenly blessings poured out upon them.

responsory.text: The blood of thy saints have they shed like water round about Jerusalem.
responsory.repeat: And there was none to bury them.

responsory.text: The dead bodies of thy servants have they given to be meat unto the fowls of the air, the flesh of thy saints unto the beasts of the earth.
And there was none to bury them.

paragraphs: Beáta es, o Béthlehem terra Juda, quæ Heródis regis immanitátem in puerórum exstinctióne perpéssa es: quæ sub uno témpore candidátam plebem imbéllis infántiæ Deo offérre meruísti. Digne tamen natálem illórum cólimus, quos beátius ætérnæ vitæ mundus édidit, quam quos maternórum víscerum partus effúdit. Síquidem ante vitæ perpétuæ adépti sunt dignitátem, quam usúram præséntis accéperint.

responsory.text: Isti sunt Sancti, qui passi sunt propter te, Dómine: víndica eos,
Víndica, Dómine, sánguinem Sanctórum tuórum, qui effúsus est.
Quia clamant ad te cotídie.

paragraphs: Blessed art thou, O Bethlehem in the land of Judah, which hast suffered the cruelty of King Herod in the slaughter of thy children; who art found worthy to offer at once to God a whole white-robed army of guileless martyrs! Surely, it is well to keep their birthday, even that blessed birthday which gave them from earth to heaven, more blessed than the day that brought them out of their mother's womb. Scarcely had they entered on the life that now is, when they obtained that glorious life which is to come.

responsory.text: These holy ones suffered for thy sake, O Lord take vengeance for them.
responsory.repeat: For day by day they cry unto thee.

responsory.text: Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints which is shed.
For day by day they cry unto thee.

paragraphs: Aliórum quidem pretiósa mors Mártyrum laudem in confessióne proméruit, horum in consummatióne complácuit; quia incipiéntis vitæ primórdiis, ipse eis occásus inítium glóriæ dedit, qui præséntis términum impósuit. Quos Heródis impíetas lactántes matrum ubéribus abstráxit; qui jure dicúntur Mártyrum flores, quos in médio frígore infidelitátis exórtos, velut primas erumpéntes Ecclésiæ gemmas, quædam persecutiónis pruína decóxit.

responsory.text: Isti sunt, qui non inquinavérunt vestiménta sua:
responsory.repeat: Ambulábunt mecum in albis, quia digni sunt.

responsory.text: Hi sunt, qui cum muliéribus non sunt coinquináti: vírgines enim sunt.
Ambulábunt mecum in albis, quia digni sunt.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Ambulábunt mecum in albis, quia digni sunt.

paragraphs: We praise the death of other martyrs because it was the crowning act of an undaunted and persistent testimony; but these were crowned at once. He That maketh an end to this present life, gave to them at its very gates that eternal blessedness which we hope for at its close. They whom the wickedness of Herod tore from their mothers' breasts are rightfully called the flowers of martyrdom; hardly had these buds of the Church shown their heads above the soil, in the winter of unbelief, when the frost of persecution nipped them.

responsory.text: These are they which have not defiled their garments.
responsory.repeat: They shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.

responsory.text: These are they which were not defiled with women for they are virgins.
They shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
They shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.

parts.title: Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Matthǽum
paragraphs: In illo témpore: Angelus Dómini appáruit in somnis Joseph, dicens: Surge, et áccipe Púerum et Matrem ejus, et fuge in Ægýptum, et esto ibi, usque dum dicam tibi. Futúrum est enim, ut Heródes quærat Púerum ad perdéndum eum. Qui consúrgens accépit Púerum et Matrem ejus nocte, et secéssit in Ægýptum: et erat ibi usque ad óbitum Heródis: ut adimplerétur quod dictum est a Dómino per Prophétam dicéntem: Ex Ægýpto vocávi Fílium meum. Tunc Heródes videns, quóniam illúsus esset a Magis, irátus est valde, et mittens occídit omnes púeros, qui erant in Béthlehem et in ómnibus fínibus ejus, a bimátu et infra, secúndum tempus, quod exquisíerat a Magis. Tunc adimplétum est, quod dictum est per Jeremíam Prophetam dicéntem: Vox in Rama audíta est, plorátus et ululátus multus: Rachel plorans fílios suos, et nóluit consolári, quia non sunt.

parts.title: Homilía sancti Hierónymi Presbýteri
parts.source: Lib. 1 Comm. in c. 2 Matth. et apud Gloss. ord.
paragraphs: Quando tulit Púerum et Matrem ejus, ut in Ægýptum tránseat, nocte tulit, et in ténebris: quia noctem ignorántiæ his, a quibus ipse recéssit, relíquit incrédulis. Quando vero revértitur in Judǽam, nec nox, nec ténebræ ponúntur in Evangélio: quia in fine mundi Judǽi fidem, tamquam Christum ab Ægýpto reverténtem suscipiéntes, illuminabúntur.

responsory.text: Cantábant Sancti cánticum novum ante sedem Dei et Agni:
responsory.repeat: Et resonábat terra in voces eórum.

responsory.text: Hi empti sunt ex homínibus primítiæ Deo et Agno, et in ore ipsórum non est invéntum mendácium.
Et resonábat terra in voces eórum.

parts.title: From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew
paragraphs: At that time, an angel of the Lord appeared in sleep to Joseph, saying: Arise, and take the child and his mother, and fly into Egypt: and be there until I shall tell thee. For it will come to pass that Herod will seek the child to destroy him. Who arose, and took the child and his mother by night, and retired into Egypt: and he was there until the death of Herod: That it might be fulfilled which the Lord spoke by the prophet, saying: Out of Egypt have I called my son. Then Herod perceiving that he was deluded by the wise men, was exceeding angry: and sending killed all the menchildren that were in Bethlehem, and in all the borders thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently inquired of the wise men. Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremias the prophet, saying: A voice in Rama was heard, lamentation and great mourning; Rachel bewailing her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.

parts.title: Homily by St. Jerome, Priest (at Bethlehem)
parts.source: Book I Comment, on Matth. II
paragraphs: He took the young Child, and His mother, and fled into Egypt, by night and in darkness; and the darkness of that night was a figure of the darkness of ignorance in which they left the unbelievers from whom they fled. But when they returned into Judaea, we learn not from the Gospel that it was by night, or in darkness; which is an image of that light which will lighten the Jews, when, at the end of the world, they shall receive back the faith, which now lighteneth the Gentiles, even as Judaea received Christ returning from Egypt.

responsory.text: The saints sung a new song before the throne of God and the Lamb.
responsory.repeat: And their voices were echoed on earth.

responsory.text: These were redeemed from among men, being the first-fruits unto God, and to the Lamb, and in their mouth was found no guile.
And their voices were echoed on earth.

paragraphs: Ut adimplerétur quod dictum est a Dómino per prophétam dicéntem: Ex Ægýpto vocávi Fílium meum. Respóndeant, qui Hebræórum volúminum dénegant veritátem, ubi hoc in Septuagínta legátur interprétibus. Quod cum non invénerint, nos eis dicémus, in Osée prophéta scriptum, sicut et exemplária probáre possunt, quæ nuper edídimus.

responsory.text: Vidi sub altáre Dei ánimas interfectórum propter verbum Dei quod habébant, et clara voce dicébant:
responsory.repeat: Víndica, Dómine, sánguinem Sanctórum tuórum, qui effúsus est.

responsory.text: Sub throno Dei omnes Sancti clamant.
Víndica, Dómine, sánguinem Sanctórum tuórum, qui effúsus est.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Víndica, Dómine, sánguinem Sanctórum tuórum, qui effúsus est.

paragraphs: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the Prophet, saying Out of Egypt have I called My Son. Those who go about to deny the authority of the Hebrew Scriptures, ask where any such passage is to be found in the Septuagint. But, although they find it not there, I tell them that the fact of its being written in the Prophet Hosea (xi. i) can be proved by the texts which I have lately published.

responsory.text: I saw under the Altar of God the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, which they held, and they cried with a loud voice
responsory.repeat: Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints, which is shed.

responsory.text: Under the throne of God all the saints cry aloud
Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints, which is shed.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints, which is shed.

paragraphs: Tunc adimplétum est, quod dictum est per Jeremíam prophétam dicéntem: Vox in Rama audíta est, plorátus et ululátus multus, Rachel plorans fílios suos. De Rachel natus est Bénjamin, in cujus tribu non est Béthlehem. Quǽritur ergo, quómodo Rachel fílios Judæ, id est Béthlehem, quasi suos ploret. Respondébimus bréviter, quia sepúlta sit juxta Béthlehem in Ephrata; et ex matérno corpúsculi hospítio matris nomen accéperit; sive quóniam Juda et Bénjamin duæ tribus junctæ erant, et Heródes præcéperat non solum in Béthlehem intérfici púeros, sed et in ómnibus fínibus ejus.

Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremias the Prophet, saying; In Rama was there a voice heard, weeping and great mourning; Rachel weeping for her children. The child of Rachel was Benjamin, and Bethlehem is not a town belonging to his tribe. We must therefore seek another reason why Rachel should weep for the children of Judah, to whom Bethlehem belongeth, as for her own. The plain answer is that she is buried at Ephrath close to Bethlehem, and she is called Mother on account of the resting-place of her earthly tabernacle being there. It is possible also that she is called Mother because the tribes of Judah and Benjamin were joined together, and Herod slew not only all the children that were in Bethlehem, but also in all the coasts thereof.

latin.heading: Quarto Kaléndas Januárii Luna vicésima. Anno Dómini 2026
entries: Cantuáriæ, in Anglia, natális sancti Thomæ, Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui, ob defensiónem justítiæ et ecclesiásticæ immunitátis, in Basílica sua, ab impiórum hóminum factióne percússus gládio, Martyr migrávit ad Christum.
Hierosólymis sancti David, Regis et Prophétæ.

Areláte, in Gállia, natális sancti Tróphimi, cujus méminit sanctus Paulus ad Timótheum scribens. Ipse autem Tróphimus, ab eódem Apóstolo Epíscopus ordinátus, præfátæ urbi primus ad Christi Evangélium prædicándum diréctus est; ex cujus prædicatiónis fonte (ut sanctus Zósimus Papa scribit) tota Gállia rívulos fídei recépit.
Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Callísti, Felícis et Bonifátii.
In Africa pássio sanctórum Mártyrum Domínici, Victóris, Primiáni, Lybósi, Saturníni, Crescéntii, Secúndi et Honoráti.
In pago Oxyménsi, in Gállia, sancti Ebrúlphi, Abbátis et Confessóris, témpore Childebérti Regis.

Viénnæ, in Gállia, Commemorátio sancti Crescéntis, Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui fuit discípulus beáti Pauli Apóstoli ac primus ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus, et cujus dies natális quinto Kaléndas Júlii celebrátur.
latin.closing: Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.

translation.heading: December 29th 2026, the 20th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
entries: At Canterbury, in England, the holy martyr Thomas, Archbishop of that see, who for his contending for righteousness and for the privileges of the Church, was smitten with the sword in his own cathedral by a band of wicked men, and so passed away to be with Christ (in the year 1170).
At Jerusalem, holy David, the King and Prophet (in the year of the world 2950).

At Arles, holy Trophimus, of whom St. Paul maketh mention in writing unto Timothy. He was ordained bishop by this same Apostle Paul, and was the first who was sent to Arles to preach the Gospel of Christ, and it was a spring, as holy Pope Zosimus writeth, whence streams of faith ran into all Gaul.
At Rome, the holy martyrs Callistus, Felix, and Boniface.
In Africa, the holy martyrs Dominic, Victor, Primian, Lybosus, Saturninus, Crescentius, Secundus, and Honoratus.
At Constantinople, holy Marcellus (of Apamea) Abbot (of the Accemeti in the year 485 or 486 in that city).

At Hiesmes, in the time of King Childebert, the holy confessor Evroul, Abbot (of the monastery of Ouche, in the diocese of Lisieux, in Normandy. He was born at Bayeux in 517, founded the Abbey of Ouche and became a monk in 567, and died on December 29, 596).
At Vienne, in Gaul, holy Crescens, the disciple of the blessed Apostle Paul and the first bishop of the said city.
translation.closing: And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.

email.html:
Thus saith the Lord: A voice was heard on high of lamentation, of mourning, and weeping, of Rachel weeping for her children, and refusing to…

Matins · Monday, 28 December 2026

Holy Innocents

Ss. Innocentium · Duplex II classis

Commemoration: Fourth day after Christmas

Read in Latin and English{{listen}}

Lesson I

Lesson from the book of Jeremias

Jer 31:15-17

Thus saith the Lord: A voice was heard on high of lamentation, of mourning, and weeping, of Rachel weeping for her children, and refusing to be comforted for them, because they are not. Thus saith the Lord: Let thy voice cease from weeping, and thy eyes from tears: for there is a reward for thy work, saith the Lord: and they shall return out of the land of the enemy. And here is hope for thy last end, saith the Lord: and the children shall return to their own borders.

℟. A hundred forty four thousand, which were redeemed from the earth; these are they which were not defiled with women. * For they remained virgins; therefore are they kings before God, and the Lamb of God is with them.

℣. These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes in the Blood of the Lamb.

℟. For they remained virgins; therefore are they kings before God, and the Lamb of God is with them.

Lesson II

Jer 31:18-20

Hearing I heard Ephraim when he went into captivity: thou hast chastised me, and I was instructed, as a young bullock unaccustomed to the yoke. Convert me, and I shall be converted, for thou art the Lord my God. For after thou didst convert me, I did penance: and after thou didst shew unto me, I struck my thigh: I am confounded and ashamed, because I have borne the reproach of my youth. Surely Ephraim is an honourable son to me, surely he is a tender child: for since I spoke of him, I will still remember him.

℟. I heard under the altar the voices of them that were slain, saying: * How long dost Thou not avenge our blood? And it was said unto them from God: Rest yet for a little season, until the number of your brethren be fulfilled.

℣. I saw under the altar of God the souls of them that were slain for the Word of God, and for the testimony which they held, and they cried with a loud voice, saying:

℟. How long dost Thou not avenge our blood? And it was said unto them from God: Rest yet for a little season, until the number of your brethren be fulfilled.

Lesson III

Jer 31:21-23

Set thee up a watchtower, make to thee bitterness: direct thy heart into the right way, wherein thou hast walked: return, O virgin of Israel, return to these thy cities. How long wilt thou be dissolute in deliciousness, O wandering daughter? for the Lord hath created a new thing upon the earth: A woman shall compass a man. Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: As yet shall they say this word in the land of Juda, and in the cities thereof, when I shall bring back their captivity: The Lord bless thee, the beauty of justice, the holy mountain.

℟. They worshipped Him That liveth for ever and ever. * And cast their crowns before the throne of the Lord their God.

℣. And they fell down upon their faces before the throne, and blessed Him That liveth for ever and ever.

℟. And cast their crowns before the throne of the Lord their God.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. And cast their crowns before the throne of the Lord their God.

Lesson IV

From the Sermons of St. Augustine, Bishop (of Hippo)

10th on the Saints

Dearly beloved brethren, today we keep the birthday of those children, who, as we are informed by the Gospel, were massacred by the savage King Herod. Therefore let earth rejoice with exceeding joy, for she is the mother of these heavenly soldiers, and of this numerous host. The love of the vile Herod could never have crowned these blessed ones as hath his hatred. For the Church testifieth by this holy solemnity, that whereas iniquity did specially abound against these little saints, so much the more were heavenly blessings poured out upon them.

℟. The blood of thy saints have they shed like water round about Jerusalem. * And there was none to bury them.

℣. The dead bodies of thy servants have they given to be meat unto the fowls of the air, the flesh of thy saints unto the beasts of the earth.

℟. And there was none to bury them.

Lesson V

Blessed art thou, O Bethlehem in the land of Judah, which hast suffered the cruelty of King Herod in the slaughter of thy children; who art found worthy to offer at once to God a whole white-robed army of guileless martyrs! Surely, it is well to keep their birthday, even that blessed birthday which gave them from earth to heaven, more blessed than the day that brought them out of their mother's womb. Scarcely had they entered on the life that now is, when they obtained that glorious life which is to come.

℟. These holy ones suffered for thy sake, O Lord take vengeance for them. * For day by day they cry unto thee.

℣. Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints which is shed.

℟. For day by day they cry unto thee.

Lesson VI

We praise the death of other martyrs because it was the crowning act of an undaunted and persistent testimony; but these were crowned at once. He That maketh an end to this present life, gave to them at its very gates that eternal blessedness which we hope for at its close. They whom the wickedness of Herod tore from their mothers' breasts are rightfully called the flowers of martyrdom; hardly had these buds of the Church shown their heads above the soil, in the winter of unbelief, when the frost of persecution nipped them.

℟. These are they which have not defiled their garments. * They shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.

℣. These are they which were not defiled with women for they are virgins.

℟. They shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. They shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.

Lesson VII

From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew

Matt 2:13-18

At that time, an angel of the Lord appeared in sleep to Joseph, saying: Arise, and take the child and his mother, and fly into Egypt: and be there until I shall tell thee. For it will come to pass that Herod will seek the child to destroy him. Who arose, and took the child and his mother by night, and retired into Egypt: and he was there until the death of Herod: That it might be fulfilled which the Lord spoke by the prophet, saying: Out of Egypt have I called my son. Then Herod perceiving that he was deluded by the wise men, was exceeding angry: and sending killed all the menchildren that were in Bethlehem, and in all the borders thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently inquired of the wise men. Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremias the prophet, saying: A voice in Rama was heard, lamentation and great mourning; Rachel bewailing her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.

Homily by St. Jerome, Priest (at Bethlehem)

Book I Comment, on Matth. II

He took the young Child, and His mother, and fled into Egypt, by night and in darkness; and the darkness of that night was a figure of the darkness of ignorance in which they left the unbelievers from whom they fled. But when they returned into Judaea, we learn not from the Gospel that it was by night, or in darkness; which is an image of that light which will lighten the Jews, when, at the end of the world, they shall receive back the faith, which now lighteneth the Gentiles, even as Judaea received Christ returning from Egypt.

℟. The saints sung a new song before the throne of God and the Lamb. * And their voices were echoed on earth.

℣. These were redeemed from among men, being the first-fruits unto God, and to the Lamb, and in their mouth was found no guile.

℟. And their voices were echoed on earth.

Lesson VIII

That it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the Prophet, saying Out of Egypt have I called My Son. Those who go about to deny the authority of the Hebrew Scriptures, ask where any such passage is to be found in the Septuagint. But, although they find it not there, I tell them that the fact of its being written in the Prophet Hosea (xi. i) can be proved by the texts which I have lately published.

℟. I saw under the Altar of God the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, which they held, and they cried with a loud voice * Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints, which is shed.

℣. Under the throne of God all the saints cry aloud

℟. Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints, which is shed.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints, which is shed.

Lesson IX

Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremias the Prophet, saying; In Rama was there a voice heard, weeping and great mourning; Rachel weeping for her children. The child of Rachel was Benjamin, and Bethlehem is not a town belonging to his tribe. We must therefore seek another reason why Rachel should weep for the children of Judah, to whom Bethlehem belongeth, as for her own. The plain answer is that she is buried at Ephrath close to Bethlehem, and she is called Mother on account of the resting-place of her earthly tabernacle being there. It is possible also that she is called Mother because the tribes of Judah and Benjamin were joined together, and Herod slew not only all the children that were in Bethlehem, but also in all the coasts thereof.

Te Deum

Martyrology

Read at Prime today, announcing tomorrow

December 29th 2026, the 20th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:

At Canterbury, in England, the holy martyr Thomas, Archbishop of that see, who for his contending for righteousness and for the privileges of the Church, was smitten with the sword in his own cathedral by a band of wicked men, and so passed away to be with Christ (in the year 1170).

At Jerusalem, holy David, the King and Prophet (in the year of the world 2950).

At Arles, holy Trophimus, of whom St. Paul maketh mention in writing unto Timothy. He was ordained bishop by this same Apostle Paul, and was the first who was sent to Arles to preach the Gospel of Christ, and it was a spring, as holy Pope Zosimus writeth, whence streams of faith ran into all Gaul.

At Rome, the holy martyrs Callistus, Felix, and Boniface.

In Africa, the holy martyrs Dominic, Victor, Primian, Lybosus, Saturninus, Crescentius, Secundus, and Honoratus.

At Constantinople, holy Marcellus (of Apamea) Abbot (of the Accemeti in the year 485 or 486 in that city).

At Hiesmes, in the time of King Childebert, the holy confessor Evroul, Abbot (of the monastery of Ouche, in the diocese of Lisieux, in Normandy. He was born at Bayeux in 517, founded the Abbey of Ouche and became a monk in 567, and died on December 29, 596).

At Vienne, in Gaul, holy Crescens, the disciple of the blessed Apostle Paul and the first bishop of the said city.

℣. And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.

℟. Thanks be to God.

Read in Latin and English

Monday, 28 December 2026

Ss. InnocentiumHoly Innocents

Duplex II classis

Commemoratio: Diei IV infra Octavam Nativitatis

Commemoration: Fourth day after Christmas

Lectio I

Lesson I

De Jeremía Prophéta

Lesson from the book of Jeremias

Jer 31:15-17

Jer 31:15-17

Hæc dicit Dóminus: Vox in excélso audíta est lamentatiónis, luctus, et fletus Rachel plorántis fílios suos, et noléntis consolári super eis, quia non sunt. Hæc dicit Dóminus: Quiéscat vox tua a plorátu, et óculi tui a lácrimis: quia est merces óperi tuo, ait Dóminus: et reverténtur de terra inimíci. Et est spes novíssimis tuis, ait Dóminus: et reverténtur fílii ad términos suos.

Thus saith the Lord: A voice was heard on high of lamentation, of mourning, and weeping, of Rachel weeping for her children, and refusing to be comforted for them, because they are not. Thus saith the Lord: Let thy voice cease from weeping, and thy eyes from tears: for there is a reward for thy work, saith the Lord: and they shall return out of the land of the enemy. And here is hope for thy last end, saith the Lord: and the children shall return to their own borders.

℟. Centum quadragínta quátuor míllia, qui empti sunt de terra, hi sunt qui cum muliéribus non sunt coinquináti: * Vírgines enim permansérunt, ídeo regnant cum Deo, et Agnus Dei cum illis.

℟. A hundred forty four thousand, which were redeemed from the earth; these are they which were not defiled with women. * For they remained virgins; therefore are they kings before God, and the Lamb of God is with them.

℣. Isti sunt qui venérunt ex magna tribulatióne, et lavérunt stolas suas in sánguine Agni.

℣. These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes in the Blood of the Lamb.

℟. Vírgines enim permansérunt, ídeo regnant cum Deo, et Agnus Dei cum illis.

℟. For they remained virgins; therefore are they kings before God, and the Lamb of God is with them.

Lectio II

Lesson II

Jer 31:18-20

Jer 31:18-20

Audiens audívi Ephraim transmigrántem: Castigásti me, et erudítus sum, quasi juvénculus indómitus: convérte me, et convértar: quia tu Dóminus Deus meus. Postquam enim convertísti me, egi pœniténtiam: et postquam ostendísti mihi, percússi femur meum. Confúsus sum, et erúbui: quóniam sustínui oppróbrium adolescéntiæ meæ. Si fílius honorábilis mihi Ephraim, si puer delicátus: quia ex quo locútus sum de eo, adhuc recordábor ejus.

Hearing I heard Ephraim when he went into captivity: thou hast chastised me, and I was instructed, as a young bullock unaccustomed to the yoke. Convert me, and I shall be converted, for thou art the Lord my God. For after thou didst convert me, I did penance: and after thou didst shew unto me, I struck my thigh: I am confounded and ashamed, because I have borne the reproach of my youth. Surely Ephraim is an honourable son to me, surely he is a tender child: for since I spoke of him, I will still remember him.

℟. Sub altáre Dei audívi voces occisórum dicéntium: * Quare non deféndis sánguinem nostrum? Et accepérunt divínum respónsum: Adhuc sustinéte módicum tempus, donec impleátur númerus fratrum vestrórum.

℟. I heard under the altar the voices of them that were slain, saying: * How long dost Thou not avenge our blood? And it was said unto them from God: Rest yet for a little season, until the number of your brethren be fulfilled.

℣. Vidi sub altáre Dei ánimas interfectórum propter verbum Dei, et propter testimónium quod habébant, et clamábant voce magna, dicéntes.

℣. I saw under the altar of God the souls of them that were slain for the Word of God, and for the testimony which they held, and they cried with a loud voice, saying:

℟. Quare non deféndis sánguinem nostrum? Et accepérunt divínum respónsum: Adhuc sustinéte módicum tempus, donec impleátur númerus fratrum vestrórum.

℟. How long dost Thou not avenge our blood? And it was said unto them from God: Rest yet for a little season, until the number of your brethren be fulfilled.

Lectio III

Lesson III

Jer 31:21-23

Jer 31:21-23

Státue tibi spéculam, pone tibi amaritúdines: dírige cor tuum in viam rectam, in qua ambulásti: revértere, virgo Israël, revértere ad civitátes tuas istas. Usquequo delíciis dissólveris, fília vaga? quia creávit Dóminus novum super terram: Fémina circúmdabit virum. Hæc dicit Dóminus exercítuum Deus Israël: Adhuc dicent verbum istud in terra Juda, et in úrbibus ejus, cum convértero captivitátem eórum: Benedícat tibi Dóminus, pulchritúdo justítiæ, mons sanctus.

Set thee up a watchtower, make to thee bitterness: direct thy heart into the right way, wherein thou hast walked: return, O virgin of Israel, return to these thy cities. How long wilt thou be dissolute in deliciousness, O wandering daughter? for the Lord hath created a new thing upon the earth: A woman shall compass a man. Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: As yet shall they say this word in the land of Juda, and in the cities thereof, when I shall bring back their captivity: The Lord bless thee, the beauty of justice, the holy mountain.

℟. Adoravérunt vivéntem in sǽcula sæculórum, * Mitténtes corónas suas ante thronum Dómini Dei sui.

℟. They worshipped Him That liveth for ever and ever. * And cast their crowns before the throne of the Lord their God.

℣. Et cecidérunt in conspéctu throni in fácies suas: et benedixérunt vivéntem in sǽcula sæculórum.

℣. And they fell down upon their faces before the throne, and blessed Him That liveth for ever and ever.

℟. Mitténtes corónas suas ante thronum Dómini Dei sui.

℟. And cast their crowns before the throne of the Lord their God.

℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Mitténtes corónas suas ante thronum Dómini Dei sui.

℟. And cast their crowns before the throne of the Lord their God.

Lectio IV

Lesson IV

Sermo sancti Augustíni Epíscopi

From the Sermons of St. Augustine, Bishop (of Hippo)

Sermo 10 de Sanctis

10th on the Saints

Hódie, fratres caríssimi, natálem illórum infántium cólimus, quos ab Heróde crudelíssimo rege interféctos esse, Evangélii textus elóquitur. Et ídeo cum summa exsultatióne gáudeat terra, cæléstium mílitum et tantárum parens fecúnda virtútum. Ecce profánus hostis nunquam beátis párvulis tantum prodésse potuísset obséquio, quantum prófuit ódio. Nam, sicut sacratíssimum præséntis diéi festum maniféstat, quantum in beátos párvulos iníquitas abundávit, tantum in eis grátia benedictiónis refúdit.

Dearly beloved brethren, today we keep the birthday of those children, who, as we are informed by the Gospel, were massacred by the savage King Herod. Therefore let earth rejoice with exceeding joy, for she is the mother of these heavenly soldiers, and of this numerous host. The love of the vile Herod could never have crowned these blessed ones as hath his hatred. For the Church testifieth by this holy solemnity, that whereas iniquity did specially abound against these little saints, so much the more were heavenly blessings poured out upon them.

℟. Effudérunt sánguinem Sanctórum velut aquam in circúitu Jerúsalem: * Et non erat qui sepelíret.

℟. The blood of thy saints have they shed like water round about Jerusalem. * And there was none to bury them.

℣. Posuérunt mortália servórum tuórum escas volatílibus cæli, carnes sanctórum tuórum béstiis terræ.

℣. The dead bodies of thy servants have they given to be meat unto the fowls of the air, the flesh of thy saints unto the beasts of the earth.

℟. Et non erat qui sepelíret.

℟. And there was none to bury them.

Lectio V

Lesson V

Beáta es, o Béthlehem terra Juda, quæ Heródis regis immanitátem in puerórum exstinctióne perpéssa es: quæ sub uno témpore candidátam plebem imbéllis infántiæ Deo offérre meruísti. Digne tamen natálem illórum cólimus, quos beátius ætérnæ vitæ mundus édidit, quam quos maternórum víscerum partus effúdit. Síquidem ante vitæ perpétuæ adépti sunt dignitátem, quam usúram præséntis accéperint.

Blessed art thou, O Bethlehem in the land of Judah, which hast suffered the cruelty of King Herod in the slaughter of thy children; who art found worthy to offer at once to God a whole white-robed army of guileless martyrs! Surely, it is well to keep their birthday, even that blessed birthday which gave them from earth to heaven, more blessed than the day that brought them out of their mother's womb. Scarcely had they entered on the life that now is, when they obtained that glorious life which is to come.

℟. Isti sunt Sancti, qui passi sunt propter te, Dómine: víndica eos, * Quia clamant ad te cotídie.

℟. These holy ones suffered for thy sake, O Lord take vengeance for them. * For day by day they cry unto thee.

℣. Víndica, Dómine, sánguinem Sanctórum tuórum, qui effúsus est.

℣. Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints which is shed.

℟. Quia clamant ad te cotídie.

℟. For day by day they cry unto thee.

Lectio VI

Lesson VI

Aliórum quidem pretiósa mors Mártyrum laudem in confessióne proméruit, horum in consummatióne complácuit; quia incipiéntis vitæ primórdiis, ipse eis occásus inítium glóriæ dedit, qui præséntis términum impósuit. Quos Heródis impíetas lactántes matrum ubéribus abstráxit; qui jure dicúntur Mártyrum flores, quos in médio frígore infidelitátis exórtos, velut primas erumpéntes Ecclésiæ gemmas, quædam persecutiónis pruína decóxit.

We praise the death of other martyrs because it was the crowning act of an undaunted and persistent testimony; but these were crowned at once. He That maketh an end to this present life, gave to them at its very gates that eternal blessedness which we hope for at its close. They whom the wickedness of Herod tore from their mothers' breasts are rightfully called the flowers of martyrdom; hardly had these buds of the Church shown their heads above the soil, in the winter of unbelief, when the frost of persecution nipped them.

℟. Isti sunt, qui non inquinavérunt vestiménta sua: * Ambulábunt mecum in albis, quia digni sunt.

℟. These are they which have not defiled their garments. * They shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.

℣. Hi sunt, qui cum muliéribus non sunt coinquináti: vírgines enim sunt.

℣. These are they which were not defiled with women for they are virgins.

℟. Ambulábunt mecum in albis, quia digni sunt.

℟. They shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.

℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Ambulábunt mecum in albis, quia digni sunt.

℟. They shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.

Lectio VII

Lesson VII

Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Matthǽum

From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew

Matt 2:13-18

Matt 2:13-18

In illo témpore: Angelus Dómini appáruit in somnis Joseph, dicens: Surge, et áccipe Púerum et Matrem ejus, et fuge in Ægýptum, et esto ibi, usque dum dicam tibi. Futúrum est enim, ut Heródes quærat Púerum ad perdéndum eum. Qui consúrgens accépit Púerum et Matrem ejus nocte, et secéssit in Ægýptum: et erat ibi usque ad óbitum Heródis: ut adimplerétur quod dictum est a Dómino per Prophétam dicéntem: Ex Ægýpto vocávi Fílium meum. Tunc Heródes videns, quóniam illúsus esset a Magis, irátus est valde, et mittens occídit omnes púeros, qui erant in Béthlehem et in ómnibus fínibus ejus, a bimátu et infra, secúndum tempus, quod exquisíerat a Magis. Tunc adimplétum est, quod dictum est per Jeremíam Prophetam dicéntem: Vox in Rama audíta est, plorátus et ululátus multus: Rachel plorans fílios suos, et nóluit consolári, quia non sunt.

At that time, an angel of the Lord appeared in sleep to Joseph, saying: Arise, and take the child and his mother, and fly into Egypt: and be there until I shall tell thee. For it will come to pass that Herod will seek the child to destroy him. Who arose, and took the child and his mother by night, and retired into Egypt: and he was there until the death of Herod: That it might be fulfilled which the Lord spoke by the prophet, saying: Out of Egypt have I called my son. Then Herod perceiving that he was deluded by the wise men, was exceeding angry: and sending killed all the menchildren that were in Bethlehem, and in all the borders thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently inquired of the wise men. Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremias the prophet, saying: A voice in Rama was heard, lamentation and great mourning; Rachel bewailing her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.

Homilía sancti Hierónymi Presbýteri

Homily by St. Jerome, Priest (at Bethlehem)

Lib. 1 Comm. in c. 2 Matth. et apud Gloss. ord.

Book I Comment, on Matth. II

Quando tulit Púerum et Matrem ejus, ut in Ægýptum tránseat, nocte tulit, et in ténebris: quia noctem ignorántiæ his, a quibus ipse recéssit, relíquit incrédulis. Quando vero revértitur in Judǽam, nec nox, nec ténebræ ponúntur in Evangélio: quia in fine mundi Judǽi fidem, tamquam Christum ab Ægýpto reverténtem suscipiéntes, illuminabúntur.

He took the young Child, and His mother, and fled into Egypt, by night and in darkness; and the darkness of that night was a figure of the darkness of ignorance in which they left the unbelievers from whom they fled. But when they returned into Judaea, we learn not from the Gospel that it was by night, or in darkness; which is an image of that light which will lighten the Jews, when, at the end of the world, they shall receive back the faith, which now lighteneth the Gentiles, even as Judaea received Christ returning from Egypt.

℟. Cantábant Sancti cánticum novum ante sedem Dei et Agni: * Et resonábat terra in voces eórum.

℟. The saints sung a new song before the throne of God and the Lamb. * And their voices were echoed on earth.

℣. Hi empti sunt ex homínibus primítiæ Deo et Agno, et in ore ipsórum non est invéntum mendácium.

℣. These were redeemed from among men, being the first-fruits unto God, and to the Lamb, and in their mouth was found no guile.

℟. Et resonábat terra in voces eórum.

℟. And their voices were echoed on earth.

Lectio VIII

Lesson VIII

Ut adimplerétur quod dictum est a Dómino per prophétam dicéntem: Ex Ægýpto vocávi Fílium meum. Respóndeant, qui Hebræórum volúminum dénegant veritátem, ubi hoc in Septuagínta legátur interprétibus. Quod cum non invénerint, nos eis dicémus, in Osée prophéta scriptum, sicut et exemplária probáre possunt, quæ nuper edídimus.

That it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the Prophet, saying Out of Egypt have I called My Son. Those who go about to deny the authority of the Hebrew Scriptures, ask where any such passage is to be found in the Septuagint. But, although they find it not there, I tell them that the fact of its being written in the Prophet Hosea (xi. i) can be proved by the texts which I have lately published.

℟. Vidi sub altáre Dei ánimas interfectórum propter verbum Dei quod habébant, et clara voce dicébant: * Víndica, Dómine, sánguinem Sanctórum tuórum, qui effúsus est.

℟. I saw under the Altar of God the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, which they held, and they cried with a loud voice * Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints, which is shed.

℣. Sub throno Dei omnes Sancti clamant.

℣. Under the throne of God all the saints cry aloud

℟. Víndica, Dómine, sánguinem Sanctórum tuórum, qui effúsus est.

℟. Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints, which is shed.

℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Víndica, Dómine, sánguinem Sanctórum tuórum, qui effúsus est.

℟. Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints, which is shed.

Lectio IX

Lesson IX

Tunc adimplétum est, quod dictum est per Jeremíam prophétam dicéntem: Vox in Rama audíta est, plorátus et ululátus multus, Rachel plorans fílios suos. De Rachel natus est Bénjamin, in cujus tribu non est Béthlehem. Quǽritur ergo, quómodo Rachel fílios Judæ, id est Béthlehem, quasi suos ploret. Respondébimus bréviter, quia sepúlta sit juxta Béthlehem in Ephrata; et ex matérno corpúsculi hospítio matris nomen accéperit; sive quóniam Juda et Bénjamin duæ tribus junctæ erant, et Heródes præcéperat non solum in Béthlehem intérfici púeros, sed et in ómnibus fínibus ejus.

Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremias the Prophet, saying; In Rama was there a voice heard, weeping and great mourning; Rachel weeping for her children. The child of Rachel was Benjamin, and Bethlehem is not a town belonging to his tribe. We must therefore seek another reason why Rachel should weep for the children of Judah, to whom Bethlehem belongeth, as for her own. The plain answer is that she is buried at Ephrath close to Bethlehem, and she is called Mother on account of the resting-place of her earthly tabernacle being there. It is possible also that she is called Mother because the tribes of Judah and Benjamin were joined together, and Herod slew not only all the children that were in Bethlehem, but also in all the coasts thereof.
